title: ～ということ — the fact that ～, the idea of ～
summary: Turns a whole sentence into a noun phrase: “the fact that ～ / the matter of ～”. It attaches to the plain form of a sentence. It is used with verbs like 知る, 分かる and 言う, and as the subject of a comment.

patterns.form: 普通形 ＋ ということ
patterns.gloss: plain form + ということ (noun and な-adjective: 休みだということ)

body.p: It packs a statement into one thing you can talk about. 彼が来ない (he isn't coming) becomes 彼が来ないということ (the fact that he isn't coming), which can take を, は or が.

body.h: Compared with the plain の / こと
body.p: Verb + こと also makes a noun phrase, but ～ということ stresses the content of what was said, heard or known. It is natural after 知る, 分かる and 聞く, and as a topic: ～ということは、～.

examples.ja: 彼（かれ）が来（こ）ないということは、もう知（し）っています。
examples.romaji: Kare ga konai to iu koto wa, mō shitte imasu.
examples.tr: I already know that he isn't coming.

examples.ja: 毎日（まいにち）運動（うんどう）するということは、なかなか難（むずか）しい。
examples.romaji: Mainichi undō suru to iu koto wa, nakanaka muzukashii.
examples.tr: The fact of exercising every day is quite difficult.

examples.ja: 店（みせ）が休（やす）みだということを、私（わたし）は知（し）らなかった。
examples.romaji: Mise ga yasumi da to iu koto o, watashi wa shiranakatta.
examples.tr: I didn't know the fact that the shop was closed.

pitfalls: Nouns and な-adjectives take だ before と: 休みだということ, not 休みということ (the latter is possible in speech but だ is the textbook form).
Do not confuse it with ～という (called ～): the word after という decides the meaning.
